prompts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a polished VISUAL GAMEPLAY CONCEPT, not implemented UI, for the Roblox game Rob A Piggy Bank. Attached screenshot is STYLE AND GAME CONTEXT REFERENCE only: cheerful very simple low-poly neighborhood, giant piggy vault, chunky rounded cream UI, dark cocoa outline, yellow buttons. Create a fresh 16:10 landscape presentation with one mobile-landscape gameplay composition, crisp readable UI large enough to judge. Small clean presentation title at top outside gameplay. In gameplay world keep pig visible in upper-middle and use lower-middle compact lock interaction tray, with empty space at lower left/right for thumb controls. Visually simple flat colored geometry and restrained bevels, Nintendo-like readable toy shapes but no existing brand logos. Bold rounded friendly type, warm ivory panels, charcoal/cocoa thick smooth outlines, canary yellow active controls, turquoise progress, pink pig accent. No realistic scratches, ornate metalwork, excessive glows, particles, chrome, painterly illustrated art or tiny text. No search field. Hide the repeated STEAL/SMASH prompts during active lock interaction. One consistent small HUD line shows target 'OLD MAN HAMM', 'LOCK LV.4'; compact payoff summary 'CARRYING 244K' and 'NEXT +310K'; compact fixed loot line 'ITEM 12%  ⓘ'. These are hypothetical sample values; bottom margin outside gameplay says 'CONCEPT • SAMPLE VALUES'. Exit/cash-out control is smaller than primary thumb action. No paid currency offers. No casino reels. Favor an actual buildable Roblox UI mockup over an infographic. Text should be sparse, large, sharp. Keep world visible and scene brighter than screenshot, with enough panel contrast. Do not recreate the current progress bars. Title 'A · POP THE PINS'. Main mechanism a chunky cutaway toy brass padlock with exactly FIVE vertical spring-loaded pin columns laid out horizontally in one compact row. First two seated pins turquoise with large check marks. Third pin yellow active, showing a clearly delineated turquoise horizontal alignment notch across its slot and a moving gold collar; tiny directional chevron makes vertical travel understandable. Last two pins muted cream/gray locked. Pins have rounded tops and visible simple zigzag spring segments, toy low-poly geometry, no realism. Show subtle numbered 1–5 labels along base. Brief instruction 'TAP WHEN THE PIN HITS THE NOTCH'. Large yellow thumb action 'SET PIN' at lower right with small keyboard E cue. Smaller cream 'TAKE & RUN' on left. Top of tray says 'PIN 3 / 5'. Make progress read from the physical pins; no separate giant progress bar. This should feel like a satisfying tactile lock-picking toy with ample breathing room, highly polished but visually simple.
